name: Parasite
blurb: Bong Joon-ho's dark comedy about a poor family that cons its way into a rich family's home
title: Parasite Explained: Plot Summary and Ending
description: Parasite (2019) explained: the Kim and Park families, the full plot from the semi-basement to the birthday party, the ending explained and its main themes.
h1: Parasite Explained: Plot, Characters and Ending
answer: Parasite (기생충, Gisaengchung) is a 2019 South Korean film directed by Bong Joon-ho, who wrote it with Han Jin-won, starring Song Kang-ho. The Kims, a family of four living in a cramped semi-basement flat in Seoul, scrape by folding pizza boxes. When the son gets a job tutoring the daughter of the wealthy Park family, the Kims see a chance and, one by one, trick their way into jobs in the Parks' elegant house. It starts as a dark comedy about class and turns into a thriller. It won the Palme d'Or at Cannes and four Academy Awards, including Best Picture, the first for a film not in English.

head: Character
Who they are

Ki-taek's wife, a former hammer-throw athlete
The Kims' son, who has failed the university entrance exam several times
The Kims' daughter, quick-witted and good at forging documents
Mr. Park's trusting wife, who runs the household
Park Da-hye and Park Da-song (Jung Ji-so, Jung Hyeon-jun)
The Parks' teenage daughter and young son
The Parks' long-serving housekeeper, who came with the house
Ki-woo's university-student friend, who tutors Da-hye

body: Beginning. Ki-woo's friend Min-hyuk brings the family a scholar's rock, said to bring wealth, and, before going abroad to study, asks Ki-woo to take over his job as English tutor to Park Da-hye. Ki-jung forges a university certificate for her brother, and Ki-woo is hired by Mrs. Park. Seeing that she is easily impressed, he recommends an art therapist, 'Jessica', for her restless young son Da-song; Jessica is Ki-jung. Ki-jung leaves her underwear in the Parks' car so that Mr. Park believes his driver has been using it for sex, and the driver is fired. Ki-taek is hired to replace him. Finally the Kims exploit the housekeeper Moon-gwang's peach allergy to convince Mrs. Park she has tuberculosis. Moon-gwang is dismissed and Chung-sook takes over. All four Kims now work in the house, pretending not to know each other, and Ki-woo begins a secret romance with Da-hye.

Middle. When the Parks go camping for Da-song's birthday, the Kims drink in the empty house. In a rainstorm, Moon-gwang rings the bell, saying she left something in the basement. Behind a shelf she reveals a hidden bunker, built by the architect who designed the house, where her husband Geun-sae has lived in secret for years, hiding from loan sharks. She begs Chung-sook to let her keep feeding him. Then the eavesdropping Kims fall into the room; Moon-gwang realises they are a family and films them on her phone, threatening to show Mrs. Park. In the middle of this the Parks call: the storm has ruined the trip and they are coming home. In a struggle, the Kims force the couple back into the bunker; Moon-gwang falls down the stairs and hits her head. While the Parks sleep on the sofa, Ki-taek, Ki-woo and Ki-jung lie hidden under the living-room table and hear Mr. Park complain about the driver's smell. They escape in the rain to find their own neighbourhood flooded, their flat under sewage water, and spend the night in a gym with other evacuees.

End. The next day Mrs. Park throws a garden party for Da-song and asks the Kims to work. Ki-woo goes down into the bunker with the scholar's rock. Moon-gwang has died of her head injury, and Geun-sae ambushes Ki-woo and smashes the rock against his head. Geun-sae then walks out into the party with a kitchen knife and stabs Ki-jung in front of the guests. Da-song, who saw Geun-sae once years earlier and thought he was a ghost, faints in a seizure. Chung-sook kills Geun-sae with a barbecue skewer. As Ki-jung bleeds, Mr. Park demands the car keys to take his son to hospital; when he picks them up from under Geun-sae's body, he pinches his nose at the smell. Ki-taek snaps, stabs Mr. Park to death and runs.

What happens: weeks later, Ki-woo wakes after brain surgery, unable to stop laughing. Ki-jung is dead. Ki-woo and Chung-sook are convicted of fraud and given probation. Ki-taek has vanished, and the police treat Geun-sae as a random homeless intruder. The house has been sold to a German family. Watching from a hill, Ki-woo sees a light flickering in Morse code: Ki-taek fled into the bunker, buried Moon-gwang in the garden at night, and now lives as Geun-sae did, sending messages up the stairs every night in the hope that his son will see them. Ki-woo writes a letter back. He promises to make a lot of money and buy the house, so that all his father will have to do is walk up the stairs. We see that scene: Ki-woo owns the house, and Ki-taek climbs up into the light and embraces his son. Then the film cuts back to Ki-woo in the semi-basement, writing the letter.

ul: The plan is a fantasy. Most viewers and critics read the final cut as the film's verdict: with no qualifications and a criminal record, Ki-woo has no realistic way to earn enough to buy a house like that, and the ending shows how unreachable that kind of wealth is.
A thin hope. Others see the letter as a sign that Ki-woo has stopped scheming and is willing to work, and that his love for his father is real, even if the plan is unlikely.
The cycle repeats. Ki-taek has become exactly what Geun-sae was, a hidden man living under a rich family's house, and the film ends where it began, in the semi-basement.

body: Why does Ki-taek kill Mr. Park? The film builds to it: the Parks repeatedly mention the Kims' smell, the smell of poverty they cannot wash off. When Mr. Park recoils from Geun-sae, a poor man dying on his lawn, Ki-taek sees the same contempt aimed at himself, and the anger he has swallowed all along comes out.

ul: Class and inequality: the rich live high on a hill in light; the poor live below street level, and the flood that ruins the Kims' home is only a ruined camping trip for the Parks.
Who is the parasite: the Kims live off the Parks, but the Parks also depend on servants they never see as people, and the poor end up fighting each other.
Smell and invisible lines: Mr. Park likes employees who never cross the line, and smell is the one sign of class the Kims cannot disguise.
Plans and chance: Ki-taek says the best plan is to have no plan, and every scheme in the film collapses under events no one could control.
Stairs and space: the film is built on staircases, with characters climbing up into wealth or descending into basements and bunkers.
Runtime: 132 minutes. Korean-language, with subtitles or dubbing; premiered at Cannes in May 2019.
Awards: the first South Korean film to win the Palme d'Or, and winner of four Oscars in 2020, Best Picture, Best Director, Best Original Screenplay and Best International Feature Film.
Versions: a black-and-white edition supervised by Bong and cinematographer Hong Kyung-pyo was released in 2020.
Content: rated R in the US; violence and bloody stabbings in the final act, some sexual content and strong language.

check.q: How does Ki-taek get the job as the Parks' driver?
options: He answers an advert in the paper
Mr. Park meets him at the pizza shop
Ki-jung gets the old driver fired by planting her underwear in the car
check.why: The Parks fire their driver for what looks like misconduct, and Ki-jung recommends her 'acquaintance' Ki-taek.

check.q: Who is hiding in the bunker under the house?
options: The architect who built the house
check.why: Geun-sae has been living there for years to escape loan sharks, fed in secret by Moon-gwang.

check.q: Where is Ki-taek at the end of the film?
options: Hiding in the bunker under the house
check.why: He fled into the bunker after the killing and sends Ki-woo messages in Morse code.

faq.q: Why is the film called Parasite?
faq.a: The Kims live off the Parks by deception, but the title cuts both ways: the Parks also live off the work of people they look down on, and Geun-sae lives in the house's hidden basement.

faq.q: Does Ki-woo buy the house at the end of Parasite?
faq.a: No. The scene of him owning the house is his imagined future; the film cuts back to him in the semi-basement writing the letter, and most readings take it as a dream he is unlikely to reach.

faq.q: What does the scholar's rock mean in Parasite?
faq.a: It is a gift that promises wealth and becomes Ki-woo's obsession with climbing up; in the end it is the weapon used against him, and he returns it to a stream.
